item.title: Luminary 0.3.0
item.description:
Early access. Smarter skipping, remembered audio and subtitles, and a player that scales with the rest of the app.
What's new - Audio and subtitles are remembered per series, including "subtitles off", and survive restarting the app. Your choice carries over to the next episode. - Skip Credits and Play Next work together. When credits start with less than 45 seconds left, the Up Next card appears (Return to skip, Shift+Return to play next). Longer credits just offer Skip Credits. - The player follows the interface size (⌘= / ⌘- / ⌘0): controls, clock, pills, menus and the Up Next card all scale. - Buttons in the player light up when you hover them, so they're easy to find on a dimmed screen. - Chapter keys: [ and ] jump between chapters. Without chapters they use the intro and credits marks, and ] on the last one goes to the end. - Esc goes back in the library, like the Back button. - The Refresh shortcut now reloads Home and library pages. Intro and credits marks stay visible on the seek bar after you've watched past them. - Faster update checks: every 4 hours, and when you return to the app.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.7
item.description:
Early access. Keeps your screen awake while you watch.
What's new - Fixed the screen turning off in the middle of a video. Luminary now keeps the display awake while a video is playing, and lets it sleep normally again when you pause or stop.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.6
item.description:
Early access. Glass by default.
What's new - The glass look is now on by default (turn it off in the account menu or Settings → General). If you switched it off before, it stays off. - In glass mode, backdrops on movie and show pages now fade smoothly into the window instead of ending in a hard line.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.5
item.description:
Early access. One more security fix.
What's new - The video player now checks your server's https certificate, like the rest of the app already did. Before, a fake server on a hostile Wi-Fi network could have picked up your sign-in token from the video stream. Plain http on your home network works as before.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.4
item.description:
Early access. No more password popups after updates.
What's new - Updates keep you signed in without macOS asking for your login password. Before installing, Luminary passes your saved sign-in to the new version, which stores it in the Keychain itself.
This update asks for your password one last time (0.2.3 doesn't have this yet): click Always Allow. From here on, updates are quiet.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.3
item.description:
Early access. Security improvements from a review of the whole app.
What's new - Public server addresses always connect with https, so your password is never sent unencrypted if https fails. Plain http still works on your home network, or if you type http:// yourself. - Hardened runtime: other programs can't inject code into Luminary to get at your sign-in. - Your sign-in token is only ever sent to your own server. - The Trailer button only opens web pages. - Signing out also clears cached artwork. - mpv's built-in add-ons (stats page, console, menus) are switched off, since Luminary has its own controls.
After updating, macOS may ask for your login password once so Luminary can read your saved sign-in. Click Always Allow.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.2
item.description:
Early access. Updates get quieter.
What's new - New versions now download in the background. When one is ready, a Restart to Update button appears at the top right of the window; ignore it and the update installs the next time you quit. Prefer to be asked first? Turn off automatic downloads in Settings → General. - The version number now shows in the top right of the window
On 0.2.1, use Luminary → Check for Updates… one last time. On 0.1.0, download the DMG below and install it like before.

item.title: Luminary 0.2.1
item.description:
Early access. A small update to test in-app updates.
If you're on 0.2.0, you don't need to download anything: Luminary offers this update itself (Luminary → Check for Updates…). On 0.1.0, download the DMG below and install it like before.
What's new - The Server box on the sign-in screen now reads "IP address or URL"

item.title: Luminary 0.2.0
item.description:
Early access. Lots of new settings to make Luminary work the way you like, and in-app updates, so this is the last version you'll need to download by hand.
Requirements: Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer), macOS 14 or newer, Jellyfin 10.9 or newer.
Install 1. Download Luminary-0.2.0.dmg below and open it. 2. Drag Luminary onto the Applications shortcut next to it (replace the old copy if asked). 3. Open it. macOS will say it can't verify the developer, because the app isn't signed with a paid Apple developer account. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway next to the Luminary message, and confirm.
Coming from 0.1.0: macOS may ask for your login password once so Luminary can read your saved sign-in. Click Always Allow.
What's new - In-app updates: Luminary checks for new versions itself (Luminary → Check for Updates…, or automatically). Updates install only if they're signed by this project. - Settings (⌘,): General, Playback, Audio/Subs, Video, Shortcuts and About - Interface size from 85 % to 150 % (⌘= / ⌘- / ⌘0) - Separate streaming quality at home and away from home - Skip intros and credits automatically, show a Skip button, or neither - Turn Up Next autoplay off, and choose when it appears - Choose skip lengths for the arrow keys and the on-screen buttons - Resume where you left off or always start from the beginning - Default playback speed, how fast the controls hide, and a volume boost limit - Preferred audio and subtitle languages, subtitle size, position and styling - HDR or always SDR, smoother color banding, hardware decoding switch - Choose which page Luminary opens to, hide watched items in libraries, and pick which Recently Added rows show on Home - New account menu at the bottom of the sidebar; long library names scroll on hover
Built with AI help and so far tested on one setup, so please open an issue if anything breaks.
